title: dedicated-gpu-pool-autoscale-breadcrumbs
content:
Quick personal notes / breadcrumbs for the dedicated GPU pool autoscaling thrash we're seeing (INC triage notes). Mostly scribbles, commands I ran and copy-paste of short logs. Use/clean as needed for postmortem.

Summary of symptom:
- Customer workloads intermittently experience high tail latency / queueing during peak; autoscaler rapidly scales nodes up then back down (thrash) and some new nodes appear healthy but GPUs not ready so pods fail or wait -> long warmup + request backlog.
- Pattern: scale up (new nodes start), scheduler places pods, pods sit in ContainerCreating or CrashLoopBackOff for 30-90s while node finishes GPU init -> autoscaler sees low CPU (or kube metrics) and scales down before pods are fully ready -> more thrash.

Hypotheses:
- Autoscaler uses wrong metric (node CPU or pending pod count) and not accounting for GPU warmup readiness or node initialization grace period.
- Node group scaleDown/scaleIn cooldown too short; health checks too eager.
- GPU driver / kubelet device-plugin sometimes reports GPUs only after containerd/kubelet restart (race on cloud-init hooks).
- StartupProbe/ReadinessProbe not used for worker pods so scheduler assumes ready and then traffic hits cold KV cache, long latency.
- Cluster-autoscaler configuration doesn't consider pod disruption budgets or node-reuse/warm-pool.

Commands I ran (timestamps local):
- kubectl get pods -n dedicated-pool --sort-by=.status.startTime -o wide | head -n 30\  (shows many in ContainerCreating / CrashLoopBackOff)
- kubectl describe pod gpu-worker-7f9c -n dedicated-pool\  (looked for events)
--- relevant events snippet:
  Events:
    Type     Reason            Age    From               Message
    ----     ------            ----   ----               -------
    Normal   Scheduled         2m     default-scheduler  Successfully assigned dedicated-pool/gpu-worker-7f9c to ip-10-0-8-45.ec2.internal
    Normal   Pulling           2m     kubelet            Pulling image "redwood/gpu-worker:prod-202602"
    Normal   Pulled            1m     kubelet            Successfully pulled image
    Normal   Created           1m     kubelet            Created container
    Normal   Started           1m     kubelet            Started container
    Warning  FailedScheduling  30s    default-scheduler  0/8 nodes are available: 8 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu.

- kubectl logs -n kube-system kubelet-ip-10-0-8-45 -c kubelet | tail -n 120  (container runtime logs)
- journalctl -u snap.nvidia-driver.service -u nvidia-device-plugin -f  (on node)
  Observed: driver installed but device-plugin logs show "no devices found" for 10-25s after node up. Then plugin re-registers and GPUs become visible.

Autoscaler / ASG checks:
- aws autoscaling describe-auto-scaling-groups --auto-scaling-group-names asg-dedicated-rtx-1
- kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep ip-10-0-8 | tail -n 20
  Observed: nodes joined but Ready status oscillates between NotReady -> Ready over ~30-90s. Instances sometimes terminated before Ready because scaleDown delay low.

Representative scheduler error when thrash occurs:
- from controller logs: "ScaleDown: node ip-10-0-8-45 is unneeded; will be terminated in 120s" followed by pods failing readiness.
- pod events: "Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu" then after device plugin re-registers pods scheduled -> but by then autoscaler already marked node unneeded.

Prometheus checks I ran (queries copied):
- rate(kube_node_status_condition{condition="Ready",job="kube-state-metrics"}[5m])
- sum(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{namespace="dedicated-pool"}) by (pod)
- avg_over_time(node_gpu_health_status[5m])  (custom metric) -> showed spikes correlating with instance boot.

Quick logs / stack snippets I saved:
- device-plugin: "no devices found in /dev for nvidia; retrying in 5s"
- kubelet: "docker runtime error: device plugin not ready; allocating 0 gpus"
- autoscaler: "low utilization detected; scaleDown candidates: [ip-10-0-8-45]"

What I tried / immediate mitigations tested (and results):
1) Increase ASG scaleDown delay on asg-dedicated-rtx-1 from 60s -> 600s (10m) and cooldown to 300s; result: briefly reduced thrash in controlled test (smoothed scale-in), but still saw capacity mismatch because nodes sometimes failed readiness >10m in worst case (rare).
2) Added node boot script to wait for /dev/nvidia* before marking cloud-init complete (small sleep-loop). Deployed to test ASG image; result: nodes now report GPUs visible faster in a subset, but I introduced ~12s extra boot time. Need canary and performance eval.
3) Created a warm-pool of size 2 (manual reserved nodes) and updated scheduler to prefer nodes labeled warm=true; result: reduced tail latency for short spikes but not scalable for longer sustained peaks.
4) Toggled cluster-autoscaler expander to "most-pods" -> no material change; problem is readiness window not accounted for.
5) Added a startupProbe/readinessProbe for gpu-worker that checks nvidia-smi and /dev/nvidia0; result: scheduler waits to send traffic until container reports ready; better but only effective once node has device-plugin working.

Outstanding questions / things to validate:
- Does our autoscaler evaluate node readiness/gpu health when considering scaleDown? It appears to use insufficient utilization heuristics only. Need to check cluster-autoscaler config flags (skip-nodes-with-local-storage, expander settings, scaleDownUnneededTime, etc.).
- Are there known race conditions in our AMI/cloud-init where device-plugin starts before driver is present? Which boot order changes are safe?
- Can we expose a node-local metric (gpu_ready=0/1) to prometheus and feed that into the autoscaler as a custom filter?
- Can we leverage AWS EC2 Warm Pools instead of keeping fully warmed nodes? Pros/cons.

Suggested longer-term fixes / experiments:
- Increase scaleDownUnneededTime to at least 10m and add a safety check that node must be Ready and gpu_ready==1 for at least 2m before considered unneeded.
- Implement warm-pool (or reserved nodes) + scale-in protection labels (e.g., node.kubernetes.io/scale-protected) for a configurable percentage of capacity (min-warm-nodes).
- Harden AMI/cloud-init: ensure nvidia driver installation is completed before kubelet/device-plugin start; add systemd ordering: nvidia-drivers.service -> nvidia-device-plugin.service -> kubelet.service.
- Add startup/readiness probes that check GPU presence (nvidia-smi) and a small inference warmup (load model small batch) if feasible. This prevents traffic hitting cold node until warmed.
- Auto-scaler change: add plugin or pre-filter: exclude nodes with gpu_ready==0 for scaleDown decisions. Consider patching cluster-autoscaler to check for a prometheus metric or k8s node annotation.

Immediate TODOs (for me / on-call):
- [ ] Create short RFC for warm-pool + scale-down window changes and route to infra-ops for review (deadline: 2026-03-05).
- [ ] Open a small infra PR to add systemd ordering for nvidia service and device-plugin (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/678) and run canary in eu-west-1.
- [ ] Add startupProbe example to gpu-worker helm chart (branch gpu-startup-probe).
- [ ] Add prometheus rule for node_gpu_ready and create grafana panel for node GPU readiness % across fleet.
- [ ] Follow up with cloud team to evaluate EC2 Warm Pools vs warm node labels (cost modelling).

Notes / context snippets from Slack/troubleshooting thread:
- @Priya: "We saw 18 scale up events in 2 hours, most reverted in <3 mins. Some customers hit 5-10s queue + 300-500ms token latency spike."
- @Samir: "Cluster-autoscaler ignored pod disruption budget because pods are not DaemonSets; scaleDown candidates chosen by low CPU not GPU."

Rough postmortem pointers (staging):
- Root cause: autoscaler scale-in policy + insufficient warmup/driver init window -> nodes terminated before GPU device plugin ready -> repeated scale events.
- Contributing factors: metrics chosen for autoscaling (CPU), missing startup probes, AMI boot ordering race.

If someone else picks this up: start with the node AMI ordering change + cluster-autoscaler scaleDownUnneededTime tweak in a canary cluster. I can provide the ASG names / PRs.

Raw copied errors saved to /tmp/gpu-autoscale-log-snips.txt on my laptop if you need exact timestamps.

End of breadcrumbs - will refine into RFC once we validate driver ordering fix.
